segments.text: Section 3. You're going to listen to a conversation between two physiotherapy
students discussing their final exams. First you have some time to look at
questions 21 to 25. Now listen carefully and answer questions 21 to 25. So what
did you think of the assessment last week? You mean the final exam? Yeah, yeah I
thought some of them were a bit hard. They were certainly tough and generally
they were very long yeah we didn't really have time to relax since they were
spread all over the week right exactly but what did you think of each test of
the six exams we did the least enjoyable for me were the two three-hour written
exams why didn't you like the written exam assessments I'm not particularly
good at writing things down like that in a short space of time and I don't
think it's a good way of testing our theoretical knowledge of physiotherapy.
I disagree, I'm afraid. I'm much keener on the written essay exams than the other
types of tests. But what about the two multiple choice exam papers in basic anatomy and physiology?
Yeah, they weren't too bad. If you didn't know the answer, all you had to do was guess.
That's okay, but I never feel comfortable with guessing. And you know that there is research
that shows that women are disadvantaged when doing multiple choice questions, compared to men.
Yeah, you've mentioned this before, but I'm not sure I believe it to be honest.
It's true. Multiple choice questions favour men rather than women. They are a male construct.
Right, if you say so.
It's not if I say so. Anyway, you have to be careful with multiple choice questions because of
the negative marking. That can really bring the score down if you keep guessing and get
all of the guesses wrong. It's double negative.
You're right, that is a danger.
What about practical exam assessments? Do you like that?
Yeah, with the volunteers, as simulated patients, I thought that was by far the best part of
the exam.
Why was that?
Well, what I liked about it was it was without risk to the patients. We had a chance to
show what we know about communicating with patients and practice our physiology knowledge
and so on.
Yes, I think I agree with you there, but I can tell you I was tired after the practice
exam with 15 test stations. It was exhausting, but also exhilarating.
I completely agree. It lasted more than three hours in total without the break.
Before listening to the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions
26 to 30. Now listen carefully and answer questions 26 to 30.
What did you think of the other two exams? The two problem-solving tests. I didn't think
I was going to handle them very well, but in the end I think they went better than I
thought they would. What I liked most was the test where we had to work in groups of five
and make adequate treatment decisions to solve a clinical problem.
That was very interesting. I'm not sure I did it very well though. Did you feel comfortable
being in a group of five and having three examiners watching you as you discussed the
problem?
Not a big problem. We did practice it several times before. You learn to forget that someone
is watching you.
But some people are better at speaking in group situations like that and they get the
best marks.
The test doesn't just assess whether people can talk a lot, it's about showing you can
interact, organise your thoughts and then demonstrate you can co-operate with other
team members.
Well, I guess we'll just have to see how it goes.
When did the results of the finals come out?
The examiners said next week.
Yeah, we've got that to look forward to then.
Why is the policy on resets?
Why?
Are you planning to fail?
No, but, well, you know what I mean.
The resets are held on 15th August, and if there is any problem after that, it goes to appeal.
We'll just have to make sure we don't fail any part of the whole examination.
I certainly won't want to try to do any of it again.
Me neither. It's hard when you are not allowed to fail any of the exams.
Yeah, I bet they don't have that policy in any other subject.
That's the end of section 3. You now have 30 seconds to check your answers. Now turn to section 4.
